generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, this one creative move runs through your studies. You might meet it in a coaching problem with no set drill, in a training-log routine that has stopped helping, or in a performance study that everyone treats as the final word. Each time, you generate a workable option, adapt it, and defend it.
generatedProse.worked-example: A sport-science student meets three things in one placement: a coaching problem with no standard drill, a training routine that has stalled, and a study everyone cites as the settled view. First he handles each on its own, with mixed results. Then he sees one creative move behind all three: try a new option, adapt it to what he observes, and defend it from the data. His coaching, his own training and his report all improve.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and sport science, creativity is most useful as one deliberate practice. Whether you are solving a coaching problem, amending a training strategy, or arguing a reading of a performance study, the move is the same: generate an option, adapt it, and defend it. It is the practice itself, repeated, that strengthens your work.

check.body: A researcher meets a stubborn problem, amends a stalled method, and argues a fresh reading of a key source, all in one project. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That creativity is one practice at work across the project: the same move of generating and defending a new option, in three different places.
_items.feedback: Yes. Attribute, self-regulation and scholarship are three faces of one creative practice.

_items.text: That the researcher was using three unrelated skills that happened to coincide.
_items.feedback: They are not unrelated. Each is the same creative move in a different arena.

_items.text: That creativity only counts when it appears in formal research.
_items.feedback: Creativity as one practice runs through everyday study too, not only research.

_items.text: That amending a method and reading a source have nothing to do with creativity.
_items.feedback: Both are creative moves: generating a better option and a fresh reading.
